finding.title: Replace unchecked e.message as String? casts in PIN dialogs with a null-safe read
finding.why: ArgumentError.message is typed Object? in dart:core, not String?. Both sites hard-cast it with `as String?`, which would throw a TypeError if PinService ever threw an ArgumentError constructed with a non-String message (e.g. ArgumentError.value(...)). Today PinService only ever throws `ArgumentError('PIN must be exactly 4 numeric digits')` so this never fires, but the cast is a landmine for the next caller of setProfilePin/setTutorPin-style methods that doesn't preserve that convention.
finding.recommendation: Use `e.message?.toString() ?? <fallback>` instead of the unchecked cast in both places.
acceptance_criteria: Both sites read e.message without an unchecked String cast
A test constructing ArgumentError.value(42, 'pin') and feeding it through does not crash

finding.title: Populate features/profiles/profiles.dart barrel exports so Rule 2 is satisfiable for the whole feature
finding.why: Every other actually-used feature barrel re-exports its public API (account.dart 21 exports, tracks.dart 26, tutoring.dart 22, progress.dart 1); profiles.dart has zero `export` statements, so its own header comment ('Import this barrel... Do NOT import deep paths directly') is impossible to follow. Grepping lib/features/**/*.dart for `features/profiles/` outside the profiles feature itself finds 65 files across 10+ other features deep-importing active_profile_provider.dart, profile_providers.dart, profile_model.dart, pin_service.dart etc. directly (plus lib/app/router/app_shell.dart, which can't even use the barrel since it exports nothing). Rule 2 is therefore 100% unenforceable for the single most cross-cut feature in the app: any future rename/move inside features/profiles/ breaks an unpredictable subset of 65+ files with no compiler-visible contract boundary.
finding.recommendation: Populate profiles.dart with export statements for the feature's actual public surface (profile_model.dart, profile_repository.dart, pin_service.dart, active_profile_provider.dart, profile_providers.dart, profile_switcher_sheet.dart, etc.), mirroring the structure already used in tutoring.dart, then migrate consumers off deep imports incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: features/profiles/profiles.dart exports every symbol currently deep-imported by 2+ other features

learning_tracker/Makefile check 15/15 (once its self-comparison bug is fixed, see the tutored_children_section.dart finding) shows a declining, tracked count of profiles/ deep imports outside the feature

finding.title: Fix Makefile check 15/15's self-comparison bug and route tutored_children_section.dart's tutoring imports through tutoring.dart
finding.why: 4 of these 5 imports (session_role.dart, tutor_grant_aggregate.dart, active_tutored_profile_provider.dart, tutor_pin_entry_gate.dart) are already exported by features/tutoring/tutoring.dart — the sibling file profile_switcher_sheet.dart in the same directory correctly imports that barrel (its line 20) for the same feature. Only manage_tutors_providers.dart (for incomingTutorGrantsProvider) is genuinely missing from the barrel. This slips past `make audit` check 15/15 because its awk script has a self-comparison bug: `match($0, ...)` matches the FIRST 'features/xxx/' substring in the whole grep output line, which is always inside the file-path field before the first colon — so the 'import feature' capture always equals the 'file's own feature' capture, and `if(a[1] != b[1])` is never true. I reproduced the exact check-15/15 pipeline by hand against the current tree: 0 lines of output, despite these 5 real violations existing right now, proving the check has never actually detected a cross-feature deep import.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk to extract the import's target feature from the substring after the first colon (not from $0, which includes the file path), not from the whole line; add `export 'package:learning_tracker/features/tutoring/presentation/providers/manage_tutors_providers.dart';` to tutoring.dart; switch tutored_children_section.dart's 5 imports to a single `import 'package:learning_tracker/features/tutoring/tutoring.dart';`.
acceptance_criteria: Running check 15/15's grep+awk pipeline against a deliberately reintroduced cross-feature deep import (negative control) prints a WARN line
After the fix, tutored_children_section.dart imports only features/tutoring/tutoring.dart for tutoring symbols

finding.title: Migrate switcherSheetPinGuardRequiredProvider to @riverpod codegen and move it to presentation/providers/
finding.why: This provider was added fresh in commit 2c346a77 ('AN-2 gate escalating actions... wave-B'), not part of the 121-usage legacy backlog the standard exempts — SM-1 explicitly says to count new additions. Every other provider in the same feature already uses @riverpod codegen (profile_providers.dart:129,137,147; active_profile_provider.dart:42). Because it's a manually-declared, non-family FutureProvider it is never autoDispose: once any widget reads it, it and its watch of profileListStreamProvider/activeProfileIdProvider stay alive for the app's remaining lifetime, not just while the switcher sheet is open. The doc comment's stated reason for going manual ('so tests can inject a known result without touching FlutterSecureStorage') doesn't require it — codegen providers are equally overridable in tests, as the neighboring codegen providers demonstrate.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite as an @riverpod FutureProvider<bool> under presentation/providers/, keeping the same override-based test seam.
acceptance_criteria: switcherSheetPinGuardRequiredProvider is annotated @riverpod and lives in lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/
an2_switcher_pin_guard_test.dart's existing overrides continue to pass unmodified
No manually-declared top-level Provider/FutureProvider remains under presentation/widgets/ in this feature

evidence.quote: /// (edit, delete, add profile, switch account, switch to adult profile) behind
/// AN-2: Escalating actions (switch to adult profile, edit, delete, switch
// The sheet renders without crashing even with pinGuardRequired=true.

finding.why: Both the widget's own class doc and this test file's header promise PIN-guard coverage for 5 escalating actions, but the test bodies only tap the per-row edit and delete IconButtons (plus one no-guard control case). Nothing taps the 'Switch account' ListTile, the 'Add Profile' ListTile, or a non-active profile row while pinGuardRequired=true. test/e2e/journeys/profiles_p1_test.dart (E2E-718, outside this batch) independently confirms the gap: its own comment says 'Full PIN challenge drive requires device integration test' and only asserts the sheet renders without crashing, never that tapping Add Profile actually raises the PIN dialog. A future refactor of _guardEscalating's call sites for these 3 actions could silently let a child-context user reach account switching or profile creation with no test catching it.
finding.recommendation: Add 3 testWidgets to an2_switcher_pin_guard_test.dart mirroring the existing edit/delete cases: tap 'Switch account', tap 'Add Profile', and tap a non-active adult profile row, each with pinGuardRequired=true, asserting find.text('Enter Parent PIN') appears.
